title.narrative: STARTFUND - Emergency response for Flood victims in the state of Rio Grande do Sul

description.narrative:
The state of Rio Grande do Sul is currently grappling with an urgent crisis triggered by heavy rains, prompting authorities to declare a state of public calamity. The crisis has escalated with updated figures indicating significant impacts. Currently, 428 municipalities, constituting a substantial portion of the state, have been affected. The humanitarian toll is severe, with 67,563 individuals seeking refuge in shelters, while 165,112 have been displaced from their homes. The overall affected population stands at a staggering 1,482,006 people. There have been 107 confirmed deaths, with 136 individuals still reported missing. Additionally, 374 people have been injured.
In response to the ongoing flooding crisis in Rio Grande do Sul, Caritas Brazil aims to address the immediate needs of the affected population, collaborating with humanitarian partners. The proposed initiative focuses on the municipality of Canoas, where severe impacts from the flooding have been observed. With an estimated 72 centers housing approximately 22,000 individuals affected by the flooding, the core strategy is to provide essential resources such as drinkable water to meet urgent needs and enhance resilience. Each affected household will receive assistance in the form of water supply, considering the average family size in the region. The Rapid Assessment Report in the affected areas reveals critical humanitarian needs, including water scarcity, food shortages, and health service requirements. Insights from community leaders underscore the pressing demand for essential resources, emphasizing the need for interventions to improve dietary diversity and access to clean water. Due to project time constraints and accessibility challenges, Caritas has chosen to focus on one primordial item, which is water, to ensure a rapid response. Special consideration will be given to the needs of vulnerable groups, such as the elderly and people with disabilities, by adapting the packaging.
